newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Establishment of a four-nation airlines will top the agenda of a diplomatic level meeting of BISTEC (Bangladesh-India-Sri Lanka- Thailand Economic Cooperation) that begins in Bangkok on Thursday.

Finance Minister S. A. M. S. Kibria said on Wednesday that the country's banking sector would experience a "dramatic improvement" in the current financial year as a result of government's corrective actions.
The government has finalised the sale of 16 state-owned enterprises.
The government has decided to set up three more export processing zones in the northern region of the country.
Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Wednesday suspended licenses of two securities companies accusing them of manipulating share price of a particular company.
China is fast becoming the largest importer of raw jute from Bangladesh outstripping the traditional importer, India.
As many as 50 international oil companies are expected to participate in next week's biddings for country's 15 open oil and gas explorations blocks.
Mr Abu Sayeed, a retired civil servant, has been chosen as the new chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission.
